request.question: What does this operator do, and how does it make money?

answer:
**Mining 360 operates an iron ore mine-to-ship business in the Pilbara, extracting and processing ore at Mine A and Mine B, then exporting it through Port Hedland Terminal to six steel-mill customers in China, Japan and Korea.** The company makes money by selling iron ore FOB (free-on-board) at the port; in Q1 FY2027 it earned **USD 509.3 M revenue** and **USD 373.1 M EBITDA** (MIXED provenance, combining SAP sales with OPS tonnage).

| Measure | Value | Unit | Period | Source |
|---------|-------|------|--------|--------|
| Ore shipped | 18.21 | Mt | FY2026 | MIXED |
| Ore processed | 19.06 | Mt | FY2026 | OPS |
| Average grade | 61.9 | % Fe | FY2026 | OPS |
| Revenue (FOB) | 509.3 | USD M | Q1 FY2027 | MIXED |
| EBITDA | 373.1 | USD M | Q1 FY2027 | MIXED |
| EBITDA margin | 80.44 | USD/t | Q1 FY2027 | MIXED |
| C1 cost | 21.09 | USD/t | Q1 FY2027 | MIXED |

The operation runs **40 haul trucks** (29 autonomous, 11 manned) across **55 fleet assets** including excavators, drills and conveyors, staffed by **1,698 people** (SAP). Iron content averages **61.9% Fe**, just below the **62% Fe** benchmark that commands premium prices (OPS). The margin chain is: mine more high-grade tonnes → keep C1 cost low → ship at benchmark grade → capture FOB revenue.

**Next step:** Monitor the three epics—cost per tonne (E1), truck failures (E2) and supplier/stock risk (E3)—because each directly threatens either tonnage or margin.

---

**Sources:**  
*SAP:* workforce (1,698 people), plant IDs (1710, 1010, 3010), customers (6).  
*OPS:* ore processed (19.06 Mt), grade (61.9% Fe), fleet (40 trucks, 55 assets).  
*MIXED:* ore shipped (18.21 Mt), revenue (USD 509.3 M), EBITDA (USD 373.1 M, USD 80.44/t), C1 (USD 21.09/t).  
*All data is simulated.*
